Ready for the maintainer to merge.

This is a SAFETY-tier review. The PR changes contour geometry and can change posted tool motion.

The joined selections pass the inside-corner tests. Both contour callers use the same offset helper. The part-clearance check remains active.

I reviewed the trial merge locally against upstream main `7bcc13a4b71df50648207acb05a4ea9c54ab258d`. The merge completed without conflicts. No GitHub runner was used.

| Local check | Result |
|---|---|
| Build: geometry, motion and app libraries, `cargo test --lib --no-run` | Passed |
| Geometry library | 47 passed |
| Motion library | 430 passed; 10 ignored |
| App library | 364 passed; 1 ignored |
| App `area_open` | 11 passed |
| App `contour_open_side` | 6 passed |
| App `contour_stock_run` | 8 passed |
| App `feature_pick_wire` | 4 passed; 1 ignored |
| App `open_band` | 7 passed |
| App `plasma_profile` | 7 passed |
| App `wire_contour` | 8 passed |
| Clippy: geometry, motion and app, `--all-targets -- -D warnings` | Passed |

I repeated two mutations in the local review worktree:

1. Restore the refusal when the swept region contains an inner hole. The bottleneck test failed: 10 passed, 1 failed.
2. Bypass the clearance check for exact offset endpoints. The short-leg test failed with a part-cut diagnostic: 10 passed, 1 failed.

After restoration, all 11 motion corner tests and all 6 app open-contour tests passed again. No mutation remains in the source.

Requested changes: none.

No golden output changed. No UI file changed, so before/after UI screenshots are not required. The decision record explains the algorithm choices.

Non-blocking note: `crates/app/src/operation/selection.rs:180` adds six lines to a file that already exceeds the 400-line guideline. The file now has 552 lines.

The full batch gate, release tests, ignored tests, interactive UI and Windows execution were not run. The reported batch failure in `microarc_test_part` was not independently checked.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: b99b4c0ecc750cdf6b3709cccb87ce73cb68bc5f -->
**Verdict: no blockers**

Independent second review (Opus, read-only). This PR is under the safety floor (2D toolpath geometry).

**Safety checks**

- Side selection: `offset_run_side` keeps only the outer CCW loop of the swept tube. Each kept point is at the offset distance from the run (within the Clipper2 arc sag). The endpoint normals go in only when `nearest_on_run(p, run).0 >= d - TOL`. Thus no kept point is nearer to the run than the offset. I did not find a path where the ride goes to the material side.
- The safety nets stay: `contour_open_run` still calls `clear_of_part` (contour_run_side.rs:76). The open boundary path still refuses a self-crossing chain (`crosses_itself`, contour_open.rs:100). The toolpath verifier still blocks the post.
- Panics and index math: no `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic!` outside tests. `n < 2` returns early before `n - 2` in `is_end_cap`. `normal_at` refuses a zero-length leg. `nearest_on_run` uses `saturating_sub`. `corner_sector_left` guards `i + 2 < n` and `i > 0`.
- Tests: the motion pins and three of the four app pins assert geometry (clearance from walls, corner points (24, 8) and (40, 8), the ride level). The `join_open_runs` unit test asserts the welded vertex lists.
- Law checks: the provenance comments are present. The Gate map line of `contour_open_side.rs` names #2277. The new test files are in the lowest crate. No snapshot PNG changes. No new crate dependency edge. The decision file has the four parts. The PR body has `Changelog:`, `Fixes #2277`, the pinning tests and "Not exercised".

**Non-blocking findings**

1. Stale text. contour_open.rs:11-13 says that a chain "whose offset folds onto itself (the buffer grows a hole ...) is refused by name, never trimmed". A hole in the buffer is now bridged and not refused. The refusal texts of the two `offset_run` wrappers (contour_open.rs:251, contour_run_side.rs, `offset_run`) still give "comes back within twice the offset" as the cause. Now they only occur when the chosen side breaks or vanishes. Update the doc and the two messages.
2. Silent leftover at a bridged mouth. When the tube bridges a narrow mouth (`an_open_run_with_a_bottleneck_notch_bridges_the_mouth`), the walls of the room behind the mouth are not cut. No note tells the user. Before this PR, the run was refused by name. The Prime Directive asks to log diagnostics and to mark partial work. Recommend a `path.notes` line when `Region::sweep` returns a CW loop. A follow-up issue (P7) is sufficient.
3. Partial duplicates. `join_open_runs` (boundary_chains.rs:97) removes only runs with the same vertex list. If the user picks an edge and also a chain that holds that edge, `group_runs` welds a chain that doubles back (for example C-B-A-B). `simple()` removes only consecutive repeats. Before this PR the CW-hole check refused such a run. Now only `material_side` and `clear_of_part` refuse it. I expect a refusal, not a gouge, but no test pins it. Recommend a test or an explicit refusal with a clear message.
4. Closed chain from open runs. `group_runs` can weld runs into a chain with `first == last` when `stitch_open_runs` leaves them open (for example at a junction with three edges). The CCW-loop filter now lets that chain through as an open run. My reading: the ride stays on the outer side and the inner side gives `Ok(None)`. Thus there is no gouge, but this case has no test.
5. File length. `crates/app/src/operation/selection.rs` is 552 lines (546 on main). The PR adds 6 lines to a file that is already over the 400-line limit. This is not new, but a split is owed.
6. Weak assert. `acute_inside_corner_and_oversized_tool_succeed_open_and_closed` asserts only zero warnings and a clean post. A clearance assert at the acute corner makes the pin stronger.
7. Coverage. The join now also applies to `PlasmaProfile` and `WireContour`. These cut open chains on the centre line, so the side is not affected. No pin covers the join for these two kinds.

Read from the diff. Not built.

The coordinator merges this PR now. It relies on the author's collaborator review 6975436568 and on the independent Opus floor review 6975855078, both on head b99b4c0ec. The non-blocking findings of the second review go into a follow-up issue.
